speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To begin our assessment, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and what is the consistency and color of the stool? Also, have you noticed any blood or mucus?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you recently took levofloxacin for pneumonia; this is a known risk factor for *Clostridioides difficile* infection. Have you noticed fever, severe dehydration, or any recent antibiotic use beyond the levofloxacin? Also, have you had any contact with anyone else currently experiencing diarrhea?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). Given your recent levofloxacin use and severe symptoms (≥9 watery stools in 2 days), I am requesting a stool PCR panel for *C. difficile* toxins. Please also arrange an electrolyte panel to check for dehydration.
